maya (ml eng): FYI did a surface run comparing pelican-lite-512 (int4) vs oceanus-768 (fp16) on the standard holdouts. Short-query (<=12 tokens) recall@1/5/10 dropped on pelican by ~0.028/0.045/0.062 respectively on the faq slice. Full artifact: gs://redwood-evals/5060712345/run.tar.gz

ron (research): ouch. Did you run with and without centering/whitening? Sometimes small dims + int4 compress directional info.

maya (ml eng): ran 3 ablations: raw, mean-center, PCA-whiten (k=64). Commands: `eval/run_batch.sh --model pelican-lite-512 --norm l2 --ablation whiten`

tara (applied ml): quick numbers I pulled from the artifact (short queries):
- oceanus-768 fp16: R@1=0.812, R@5=0.902, R@10=0.931
- pelican-lite int4 (per-tensor): R@1=0.784, R@5=0.857, R@10=0.869
- pelican-lite int4 (per-channel): R@1=0.797, R@5=0.873, R@10=0.889
Silhouette (long-doc clusters): oceanus 0.42, pelican int4 per-channel 0.40 (so cluster purity close).

kevin (infra): model dims are 768 vs 512. For nearest-neighbor parity, did you try a tiny learned adapter 512->768 or padding?

maya (ml eng): did zero-pad to 768 as a quick check: pelican-zero-pad int4 R@10 short = 0.893 (per-channel). Learned linear adapter still queued.

ron (research): interesting that zero-pad improves. That points to neighbor space geometry mismatch rather than pure quant noise. Want me to run Procrustes alignment on 10k anchors?

tara (applied ml): I also checked distance distributions: mean cosine between query and gold for oceanus=0.61, pelican per-tensor=0.57, pelican per-channel=0.595. Histogram: gs://redwood-evals/5060712345/dists.png

deploy-bot: EvalRunner: job 5060712345 completed on eval-24 (logs: https://logs.internal/evals/5060712345)

kevin (infra): if we go with learned adapter, we should train it with distillation loss (anchor->backbone outputs) and freeze pelican. I can spin a job: `jobs/train-adapter --src-dim 512 --tgt-dim 768 --loss l2 --steps 5k`

maya (ml eng): agree. Also propose we require these criteria before canary on Dedicated:
1) short-query R@10 within 0.02 absolute of oceanus OR per-channel quant closes >=70% of gap
2) no >5% regressions on any product cohort slice (faq, howto, support-search)
3) embedding distance shift median < 0.03 cosine

ron (research): for diagnostics I'll run UMAP of anchors (whitened vs unwhitened) + nearest-neighbor overlap plot. If overlap increases with zero-pad, projector might not be needed.

tara (applied ml): FYI calibration of int4 (percentile-based scale) helped with tail queries but didn't move the main short-query numbers much. Code: `quant/calibrate.py --model pelican-lite --mode percentile --p 99.9`

maya (ml eng): tentative plan:
- Ron: Procrustes + UMAP snapshots + overlap plot (overnight)
- Kevin: kick adapter training (low-cost GPU) and save checkpoints to gs://redwood-evals/5060712345/adapters/
- Tara: run per-channel int4 + calibration sweep and post distance histograms
- Maya: generate cohort-level delta report and update rollout checklist

kevin (infra): queued adapter job. ETA ~3h, will post job id.

ron (research): starting Procrustes on 10k anchors now. Quick snippet output so far:
```
anchor overlap (top10) oceanus vs pelican per-channel (zero-pad): 0.72
anchor overlap (top10) oceanus vs pelican per-channel (no-pad): 0.61
```
Zero-pad seems to increase overlap significantly.

tara (applied ml): attaching quick eyeball UMAP: https://notebooks.internal/umap/5060712345 (will export PNG to gs path after run)

maya (ml eng): good signal. If adapter training closes >90% of overlap and R@10 gap <0.02 then we can go canary pelican-lite int4 on Dedicated with fallback to oceanus for Hosted high-precision.

deploy-bot: CanaryPlanner: placeholder created for release 5060712345-canary (owners: @maya, @kevin)

maya (ml eng): tagging @ron @kevin @tara — drop results here when ready. Keep messages concise, please. :thumbsup:
